questions.question: Which locator is the best first choice for a Save button?
questions.explanation: Role and accessible name describe what a user perceives, so the locator keeps working when classes or layout change.

questions.question: A test must read the response that a Save click triggers. Where does `page.waitForResponse()` belong?
options: Start it before the click, and await its promise after the click
Await it on the line after the click
Await it on the line before the click
questions.explanation: A wait only sees events that happen after it starts. Awaiting it first would stall before the click, and starting it after the click can miss a fast response.

questions.question: A click opens a `confirm()` dialog and the test has no dialog listener. What happens?
options: The test hangs until it times out
Playwright dismisses the dialog, so `confirm()` returns `false`
Playwright accepts the dialog, so `confirm()` returns `true`
questions.explanation: Without a listener Playwright dismisses dialogs automatically. A test that needs OK must register a handler that calls `dialog.accept()` before the click.

questions.question: How do you click a Pay button inside `<iframe id="pay">`?
questions.explanation: An iframe holds a separate document, so page locators can't see inside it. A frame locator scopes the search to that frame.

questions.question: A button sits inside an open shadow root. Which locator will not find it?
questions.explanation: CSS, text, and role locators pierce open shadow roots automatically. XPath doesn't.
